questions.q: What is the real distinction between system settings and personal preferences?
options: There is no real distinction — they are the same thing
System settings apply instance-wide (or to a role); personal preferences apply only to the individual user who set them
Personal preferences apply instance-wide; system settings apply only to one user
Both only apply to administrators
questions.explain: System settings affect everyone or everyone with a given role; personal preferences affect only that one user's own experience.

questions.q: Where do system-wide settings primarily live?
options: The user's profile picture or user menu
Behind the gear/settings icon, or more fully in the System Properties application
In the Application Navigator's History view
They don't live anywhere configurable
questions.explain: System Properties and the gear icon hold instance-wide configuration, typically restricted to administrative roles.

questions.q: Which of these is a personal preference rather than a system setting?
options: Default list page size for the whole instance
A user's own display time zone
Whether a module is enabled for every user
Session security configuration
questions.explain: Time zone, language, notifications, and theme are per-user preferences — they don't touch any other user's session.

questions.q: Why is System Properties typically role-gated, while personal preferences generally are not?
options: Because personal preferences don't actually exist
Because a careless change to a system property affects the whole instance or a whole role, not just the person making it
Because System Properties is only cosmetic and has no real effect
Because personal preferences require administrator role to change
questions.explain: System-wide changes carry wider blame radius, which is exactly why they're gated behind admin roles, unlike a user's own preferences.

questions.q: A new agent says incident timestamps "look wrong" on their own screen only. What's the most likely fix?
options: Change a system-wide date/time property in System Properties
Check and adjust that agent's personal time zone preference in their own profile menu
Disable the Incident application for the whole instance
Nothing can be done about display timestamps
questions.explain: A display issue affecting only one user's own screen points to their personal time zone preference, not an instance-wide system setting.
